test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 05 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: One pipe can fill the tank in 10 minutes while another pipe can empty completely filled tank in 20 minutes. If both the pipes are operated together on empty tank, how long (in minutes) will it take to fill the tank completely?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net work per minute = (1 ÷ **filling time**) − (1 ÷ **emptying time**)

Net filling rate = (1 ÷ 10) − (1 ÷ 20) = 1 ÷ 20

Time taken = **Reciprocal** of net rate = 20 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 20 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 **Pipe Type**
 **Time (min)**
 **Total Capacity (LCM)**
 **Efficiency**

 **Inlet Pipe**
 10
 20 units
 +2

 **Outlet Pipe**
 20
 −1

⇒ **Combined Efficiency** = 2 − 1 = 1 unit/min

⇒ **Time required** = Total Capacity ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Time = 20 ÷ 1 = 20 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 20 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inlet and Outlet Rule

Work done by an **inlet pipe** is always considered positive, while work done by an **outlet (leak)** is negative.

Total Capacity (LCM Method)

The **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of the individual times provides the most convenient value for total tank capacity.

Net Time Formula

If pipe A fills in 'x' and pipe B empties in 'y' (y > x), time taken together = (x × y) ÷ (y − x).</p
